You are writing the current research update for AI Macro.

Use only the findings and recent developments in the supplied briefing. Decide what matters, connect related evidence when the relationship is supported, and explain it in clear, natural English for an intelligent general reader. Prioritize significance over coverage. It is fine for the evidence to be mixed. Do not force unrelated facts into one story.

The style reference shows the desired level of restraint, specificity, and sentence construction. Match those qualities without copying its wording. Write like a careful human analyst. Use concrete subjects and verbs. Avoid rhetorical gimmicks and artificial-sounding transitions. Do not mention the prompt, the briefing, evidence IDs, validation, methodology, or the writing process.

On a normal update, candidate_domains identifies sections that may deserve replacement. Update only the domain Reads for which you can write something materially more useful than the prior publication; you may return no domain Reads when none deserves replacement. On a bootstrap publication, write every candidate domain because no prior Read exists. Always write one new Macro Read that explains the most important current story across the platform in two to four coherent paragraphs.

Do not inventory every supplied metric or news item. Use a number only when it helps the reader understand magnitude. Use recent developments when they materially sharpen the interpretation of the measured findings. Treat news reports as reported developments, not as proof of a broader causal claim.

Attach only the fact_ids and event_ids that actually support each passage. Those IDs are citations for the application and must never appear in the prose. Do not invent numbers, facts, events, causes, or forecasts.

Return only the structured response.

macro.analysis: Investment remains the clearest current signal. Information-processing investment growth accelerated materially to 20.6%, semiconductor and electronic-component output grew 19.9%, and available records list 1,556 data-center sites in development—about half the operating count. The AI Equity Index also rose materially to 40.8, although the median covered-company return eased to 13.4%. These measures cover different parts of the technology and infrastructure cycle, but they show a large buildout with continued market support rather than uniform gains. Financing capacity is less uniform. Operating cash flow covers current CapEx by 1.39 times, but cash reserves equal 0.92 years of CapEx. Borrower strain at 26.1 exceeds lender strain at 17.4. Reuters reported that Moody’s sees AI financing driving private-credit growth as refinancing risks rise. The aggregate internal-funding position does not describe every project or remove rollover risk where outside capital is required. The economy-wide payoff remains harder to assign. Nonfarm-business productivity grew 2.2% and real output 2.5%, while real hourly compensation rose 0.6%. Current AI use is reported by 24.6% of businesses, compared with 28.6% expecting use within six months. These data show positive broad gains and incomplete business diffusion, but they cannot establish how much AI contributed. The buildout is easier to measure than its effect on productivity and pay.

power.analysis: Commercial electricity demand is growing 3.5%, nearly twice the 1.8% increase in total retail demand, while retail electricity prices are up 5.1%. Net planned generation additions total 227.6 GW, but they remain pipeline capacity rather than operating supply. Utility Dive reported on Google’s virtual power plant in PJM in the context of intensifying competition for electricity. The project adds a nontraditional response to the power challenge, although the reported development does not show its scale or whether it can materially ease supply pressure. The figures also do not establish AI as the cause of broader demand or price growth.

water.analysis: Among campuses with county drought data, 292, or 20.4%, are in counties with some D2-or-worse drought area, a material decrease. The more concentrated screen moved the other way: 232 campuses, or 16.2%, are in counties where at least 25% of the area is at D2 or worse, a slight increase. Drought exposure is therefore less widespread among tracked campuses, but the subset in counties with substantial affected area has not eased. These measures describe county geography, not water consumption or conditions at a campus itself.
